$comment: 🧠️ The graph memo: the slice a graph planner child produced once, kept beside the change journal and served again to the next identical request while the journal proves that nothing the planned generation read has changed. `relevance` is the closed table of what a fact row reads: `path` rows read the entry they name, `none` rows read nothing of the tree, `link` rows follow symbolic links, `resolve` rows resolve a request, `text` rows name their inputs inside their key. A kind this table does not name makes a generation unsealable (fail closed); a law keeps the table equal to the kinds the observation and generation schemas declare. Stamp refinement: the discovery frontier of a generation holds, per directory, the entry stamp (mtime, inode) captured with it; the planner itself treats a directory with an unmoved stamp (and not touched within the racy window of the capture) as one whose names, node types and absences cannot have moved (`stableDirectoriesV1`). A directory of the frontier whose facts are only entries and listings of kinds `Policy.stamped` is STAMPED: a row that adds, removes or renames a name directly inside it is relevant, a row that only says 'modified' (a content edit of a sibling no fact read; the kind is advisory) is settled by one lstat against the stamp kept in the table `.lst`. Directories a resolution or derived fact names, directories read by a kind of `Policy.following` (it follows symbolic links), and directories without a usable stamp are STRICT: every row directly inside is relevant (except the modification of a directory). `carry`: a sealed slice whose generation pointer moved is served under the newer generation when every generation-wide digest named in `shared` and the row of every owner the slice covers are identical in both manifests (the planner would verify the same facts and assemble the same projects from the same rows); otherwise the reason `pointer` names the first difference. Edit refinement: when the journal names a relevant change, the memo does not give up at once. The edit index of the sealed sidecar maps every entry to the rows that name it and every directory to the rows that read its children; the lookup re-checks exactly those rows with the planner's own checks (an analysis is replayed and compared by its result, so an edit that keeps a file's imports and modules holds), proves a directory that has relevant entries below it to be the same directory (frontier inode), lists a frontier directory whose children changed again with the planner's own walk predicates and compares its subdirectories and members, refuses a touched path that became a symbolic link, a row it cannot check (a derived fact, a closure) and more than `maximumEditPaths` paths or `maximumEditRows` rows; when everything holds it serves and re-seals the stamps of the directories it listed again. Derived refinement: a re-checked row that does not hold and that only pseudo owners hold (the support of derived facts), and a derived fact the journal names, make the memo ask those questions again with the planner's own derivation (`openGenerationDeriverV1`, `settleSuspectsV1`) in a child process of the same invocation (`Policy.derive`); it serves only when every answer is the recorded one and every new support reads only entries the old support read; a stale row a project or the environment holds itself, a failed or changed answer, a new entry and more than `maximumDerivedQuestions` questions plan. Outputs: a directory named in `Policy.outputs` is one a build writes its own results into (the git-ignored `.🧾️store`: temp file, lock directory, rename on every build). Its listing facts are not vouched for by the journal but re-checked by the engine on every lookup (they join the recheck set), and the directory is neither strict nor stamped; a row that names an entry or an ancestor is still relevant, a row directly inside is settled by the recorded listing. Assumption declared with the list: the graph takes no project, member or entry from such a directory.

en.served: graph: {projects} projects served from the memo of {seconds} s ago; the journal vouches for {rows} facts and {rechecked} facts outside its sight held, no planner process was started
en.refused: graph: the memo cannot serve this request ({reason}); the graph is planned
en.carried: graph: the memo of generation {from} still describes generation {to}: the {projects} projects it serves are unchanged there
en.edited: graph: the memo re-checked the {rows} facts that read the {paths} changed paths with the planner's own checks; they all still hold
en.derived: graph: {questions} derived facts that read them were asked again by a child process with the planner's own derivation; every answer is unchanged

de.served: graph: {projects} Projekte aus dem Memo von vor {seconds} s geliefert; das Journal bürgt für {rows} Fakten, {rechecked} Fakten ausserhalb seiner Sicht gelten noch, es wurde kein Planer-Prozess gestartet
de.refused: graph: das Memo kann diese Anfrage nicht bedienen ({reason}); der Graph wird geplant
de.carried: graph: das Memo der Generation {from} beschreibt auch Generation {to}: die {projects} gelieferten Projekte sind dort unverändert
de.edited: graph: das Memo hat die {rows} Fakten, welche die {paths} geänderten Pfade lesen, mit den Prüfungen des Planers nachgeprüft; alle gelten noch
de.derived: graph: {questions} abgeleitete Fakten, die sie lesen, wurden von einem Kindprozess mit der Ableitung des Planers neu befragt; jede Antwort ist unverändert

edit.$comment: The edit index of the sealed relevance (`id` = sha256 of the `.rix` file) and the fact index and frontier of the generation it was computed from: `index` names the rows by their position in that fact index, so a lookup fetches exactly the rows it re-checks from the immutable generation store; a retired index makes the memo plan.

state.$comment: light: the slice and the generation it served, kept after the first planner run; sealed: with the relevance of the generation, written by the run that found the same slice again, in the same generation or in a newer one whose rows of the slice are identical (Policy.carry), so the sealing cost is paid only by a repeated request, never by an edit-and-run loop.

Sidecar.$comment: The relevance of ONE served slice: `rows` counts the fact rows of the owners the served pin covers, of the environment owner and of the pseudo owners that support their derived facts (the selection the planner verified before it served the slice); a stale fact of an owner outside the slice never refuses it. A missing or foreign pin makes the sidecar unsealable (`pin`, `other-generation`). A slice the planner did not verify after the memo's journal cursor (served from a peer's verified stamp or from the pin of an outer invocation) is unsealable too (`unverified`): the sealing child is started with `requestedAt` set to the clock time right after the cursor, so a stamp serves it only when its observation began after the cursor, and the pin it records must not be older than that time.

edit.$comment: Written by the sealing child next to the relevance: `index` and `frontier` are the digests of the fact index and of the frontier of the served generation, `stem.rix` holds the edit index (the rows that name each entry, the rows that read the children of each directory, the directories with something relevant below them, the frontier directories and members).

DeriveRequest.$comment: Written by the memo for its derivation child (`Policy.derive` names the file): the fact index of the sealed generation and the pseudo owners whose derived question the child asks again.

DeriveAnswer.$comment: Written by the derivation child next to the request (`.answer.json`): `held` the questions whose answer is the recorded one and whose new support reads no entry the old support did not read, `changed` the questions whose answer moved, `failed` the computations that failed, `uncovered` the held questions whose new support reads a new entry (the memo's relevance does not watch it), `missing` when the fact index is no longer retained.
